finding.claim: The dispatch's own headline ("804,497 parcel-node atoms vs 500,307 CAD prop_ids = 304,190 unexplained") is itself an instance of DEV_PROCESS rule 1.3 (measure the class, never derive by subtraction). The real reconciliation is a three-way split, not one residual bucket, and the true excess (423,580) is larger than the naive subtraction (304,190) because true overlap (380,917) is smaller than either total.

evidence.instrument: count(distinct entity_id), count(distinct body->>'parcelNodeId'), count(*) over atoms WHERE entity_type='parcel-node' AND countyFips='48453'
evidence.result: 804,497 / 804,497 / 804,497 -- every row is a genuinely distinct parcelNodeId; the divergence is not duplicate atoms per parcel.

evidence.instrument: Exported and diffed (sort/comm) the full Travis parcel-node atom id set against the full Travis cad_property distinct prop_id set
evidence.result: overlap (real, CAD-backed, ring-bearing) = 380,917; CAD prop_ids with no parcel-node atom = 119,390 (the same set as F1/F3's no-ring gap); parcel-node atoms with no matching current CAD row = 423,580 -- this is the true excess, 119,390 more than the dispatch's naive-subtraction number.

evidence.instrument: Length/prefix inspection of the 423,580 unmatched ids
evidence.result: 423,540 (99.99%) match the pattern `_feature-stratmap25-landparcels-48453-travis-202508-<seq>` -- a documented synthetic key, not a stale numeric prop_id. Only 40 are plain numeric ids, and those 40 are status='retired' already.

SYNTHETIC_PARCEL_KEY_PREFIX = '_feature-' is a documented, tested, intentional fallback identity for a StratMap polygon feature the writer could not resolve to a real CAD account. reconcile-county-parcel-nodes.ts exists specifically to retire synthetic keys from a superseded vintage (invariant S2), but its mechanism is a vintage-transition diff -- it has nothing to diff against while a county has only ever had one ingested vintage.

evidence.instrument: SELECT body FROM atoms WHERE parcelNodeId LIKE '48453:_feature-stratmap25-landparcels-48453-travis-202508%' AND status='active' LIMIT 1
evidence.result: body carries an honest, self-documenting absence: {"kind":"parcel-key-unresolved","reason":"every tier failed for this parcel -- no usable prop_id token (value \"0\"); ... no usable geo_id_crosswalk token (value \"0\") ..."}. fetchedAt/evaluatedAt = 2026-09-07T14:58:22Z (today, likely from the same-day PR #396/#397 crosswalk-cascade apply CTX-E's CP1 independently documents on origin/main).

evidence.instrument: SELECT source_vintage, count(*) FROM txgio_parcel WHERE county_fips='48453' GROUP BY 1
evidence.result: Exactly one vintage on file: stratmap25-landparcels_48453_travis_202508 (894,657 raw polygon features). 894,657 = 380,917 (resolved to a real CAD account) + 423,540 (parcel-key-unresolved, source prop_id/geo_id token literally '0'/blank) + a small remainder. Confirms 804,497 counts every ingested StratMap polygon feature, resolved or not -- not a proxy for parcel count.

finding.secondMechanismConsidered: Stale prior-CAD-tax-year prop_ids (2025 vs 2026 vintage) was the first hypothesis, prompted by cad_property's own 2025/2026 tax_year split (380,918 / 492,848 distinct prop_ids) landing suspiciously close to the 380,917 overlap figure. Rejected on direct inspection: the unmatched ids are not numeric at all (they are the `_feature-stratmap25-...` synthetic key), and cad_property_vintage_crosswalk (the table that would carry a real prop_id-renumbering fact) has 0 rows for Travis -- there is no renumbering event to invoke.
finding.conclusion: Not a writer bug and not literally 'unexplained' -- the atom store already carries the mechanism, per-row, in its own absence field. The genuine gap is operational, not code-level: 423,540 Travis parcel-node atoms have sat in status=active with a self-declared parcel-key-unresolved absence since the only ingest Travis has ever had (Aug 2025), and any consumer that reads 'parcel-node atom count' as a proxy for 'real parcel count' for Travis will overcount by ~85%. The correct denominator is cad_property's distinct prop_id count (500,307), not the atom count.
